current.text: He signed a new contract with Utah.
Experts expect him to start at point guard. Josh says he has looked really good in the preseason.
Utah has Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. for a full season and added rookie Darryn Peterson. The projected starting lineup is George, Peterson, Markkanen, Jackson and Jusuf Nurkic.

His usage is expected to drop with Markkanen, Jackson and Peterson sharing the ball. He may lose about one assist per game, and Leaf does not expect him to repeat 23.6 points per game. Experts still expect him to be good.
Leaf says that as his volume drops, he needs to learn to play and shoot off the ball or become a big distributor.

Experts think the market undervalues him. Lloyd finds his ESPN category rank of 89 strange and doubts last season was a fluke. Another expert says a Fantrax ADP of 58 overdoes his expected usage drop.
In category mock drafts, experts took him in round 5, around picks 48 to 58. In an auction mock he went for 20 USD, which Josh called reasonable.
In an ESPN points league mock, one speaker said pick 108 was too early for him. That call is for a points format, not ours.
Josh expects Utah's minutes and usage to be all over the place early in the season.
Utah is expected to try to win this season. Leaf projects 43 wins and a 7th or 8th seed, with a top 10 offense. Experts say tanking and shutdown fears are misplaced.

durable.text: Turnovers are his weak category. He commits many for a guard.
His strengths are FT% on good volume, assists and points.
His rim finishing rose from 54 to 65 percent. One expert thinks he can keep that level.
He is not a good defender.

note: The market is split on him. Yahoo values him at 23 USD but his average Yahoo cost is only 12.3 USD, and ESPN values him at 3 USD. Experts treat him as a round 5 category target worth about 20 USD, and our league paid only 2 USD for him last season. He fits punt TO builds best because his FT%, assists and points hold value. Early on, check how much usage he keeps next to Peterson, Markkanen and Jackson, and whether his FG% stays near last season's 45.6%. The projections range from 44.3% to 47.5%.
